The input-end voltage is labeled v(t). The lower half gives the waveform of v(t) versus time: there is an initial constant plateau between t=0 and τ, then it changes at τ, and approaches the steady-state level indicated by the dashed line near 2τ. Reasoning: During the initial time interval from 0 to τ, the source end has not yet received the reflection from the far-end load, so this finite-length lossless line looks equivalent from the input end to a semi-infinite transmission line, whose input impedance equals the characteristic impedance Z0 = 100 Ω. At this time, the input-end voltage is determined by the voltage division formed by Thevenin source A, series resistance R_Th, and equivalent load 100 Ω: v(0+) = A·100/(R_Th + 100). According to the normalization relation between the initial plateau in the figure and the source step amplitude, the initial input voltage is A/2. Therefore A·100/(R_Th + 100) = A/2. Canceling A gives 100/(R_Th + 100) = 1/2, so R_Th + 100 = 200, R_Th = 100 Ω.
